ksp_mappings.explanation: Source messaging KSP1 is about convertible design, AI power, and leaders sketching, presenting, and collaborating. Because the two documents conflict on product identity and the convertible/sketch use case is product-dependent, it is mostly omitted from scored prompts; only broad professional work context survives where independently compatible.
Source messaging KSP2 supports confident meetings. It contributes modestly to office prompts with meeting notes, but device-specific camera and audio claims are not visualized.
Source messaging KSP3 supports secure, manageable, IT-friendly business context. It contributes only broad professional/work-anywhere context, not specialized IT-management scenes.
Source messaging KSP4 is sustainability-focused. It does not naturally become an ordinary C-Tech environment prompt, so recycled-material claims are omitted from the scenes.

value_proposition.explanation: Both documents support a premium mobile business-computing story for professionals, leaders, meetings, security, and work across locations. Because the documents name different product identities, the prompts avoid device-dependent claims and rely on shared compatible lifestyle cues such as offices, home work, meetings, papers, and shared work settings.

debug.input_assessment: The smart brief is rich in scene cues: offices, home, travel, shared spaces, meeting-heavy days, documents, briefings, executives, and hybrid work. Source messaging is also rich but describes a different Flip product with 2-in-1, touch, optional pen, and sketch/present modes, so product-dependent use cases were handled cautiously. The camera tag resolves exactly to a medium oblique laptop view with two local props and one background detail allowed.
debug.count_explanation: Generated exactly 20 distinct prompts. The set covers Home, Office, Education, Gaming, Café, and Creative Studio. Candidates are sorted by descending source relevance score, then by descending C-Tech reference score within ties.
ignored_fields: Source-messaging authoring instructions such as checking NPI Content Factory and legal-copy usage requirements were treated as document metadata, not prompt instructions.
BrightEdge rankings, URLs, and data warnings were not used as lifestyle scene evidence.
Disclaimers, footnotes, operating-system requirements, technical specifications, and service availability statements were not converted into scene props.
Target-device brand, model, device type, appearance, ports, screen, and state were excluded from all prompt text.
debug.diversity_summary: The bank emphasizes source-grounded home and office work first, then source-adjacent cafés and creative studios, followed by required education and gaming creative departures. Diversity comes from C-Tech reference environments and ordinary surfaces: wooden home desks, corporate desks, integrated shelving, café tables, creative-office tables, library/classroom study surfaces, and dark gaming desks.
limitations: No people were added, even though the resolved camera allows optional partial activity, because the C-Tech references do not require people.
The resolved medium camera limited local props to two and background details to one, requiring substantial deletion from wide C-Tech references.
Product mismatch limits use of source-messaging-specific Flip, 2-in-1, tablet, tent, touch, and optional pen scenarios.
Education and Gaming are required environment families but are not supported by the provided source documents, so they are marked as creative departures.
